research_text:
## Finding and API meaning

`javax.crypto.spec.PBEKeySpec` represents a user-chosen password and, depending on the constructor, parameters used to generate a password-based encryption key. Oracle documents the **three-argument constructor** for fixed-key-size PBE ciphers and the **four-argument constructor** for variable-key-size PBE ciphers. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/spec/PBEKeySpec.html?utm_source=openai))

The quoted `ForbiddenMethod` message refers to the **three-argument constructor call**, not to a particular iteration-count value. The supplied description of a possible low count in a *four-argument* call is a separate detector claim; it is not established by that forbidden-method message. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/PBEKeySpec.crysl))

## Exact CrySL rule

The published rule declares `SPEC javax.crypto.spec.PBEKeySpec`. Its matching clause is, verbatim: ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/PBEKeySpec.crysl))

```crysl
FORBIDDEN
	PBEKeySpec(char[]) => Con;
	PBEKeySpec(char[],byte[],int) => Con;
```

- The clause specifies **constructor name and parameter types**: one `char[]`, or `char[]`, `byte[]`, and `int`. Constructors have no receiver. The file also declares the four-argument `PBEKeySpec(...)` event and the no-argument `clearPassword()` event under the specified API class.
- **The forbidden clause has no additional value condition.** Separately, the file specifies the four-argument event as `Con`, orders it before `clearPassword()`, and lists `iterationCount >= 10000`, password constraints, and `randomized[salt]`.
- **A name alone is not what this rule declares:** it identifies the governed class and parameter signatures, not an arbitrary same-named method on another type. The file does not itself specify an analyzer’s method-resolution implementation, so it cannot establish whether a particular analyzer might nevertheless report an unrelated same-named call. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/PBEKeySpec.crysl))

Rule source, on the mutable `master` branch:  
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/PBEKeySpec.crysl

The retrieved file’s SHA-256 was **not independently verified** against the hash supplied in the question.

## Documented usage and remediation limits

Oracle documents both the three- and four-argument constructors; it does **not** call the three-argument constructor forbidden. For either, the salt must be non-null and nonempty and the iteration count positive. For the four-argument constructor, the requested key length must also be positive. A null password is treated as an empty password. Password and salt inputs are cloned. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/spec/PBEKeySpec.html?utm_source=openai))

Oracle recommends collecting sensitive passwords in a `char[]`, rather than an immutable `String`. `clearPassword()` clears the specification’s internal password copy; callers are responsible for zeroing copies returned by `getPassword()` when no longer needed. Oracle’s PBE example uses a `SecureRandom`-generated salt. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/spec/PBEKeySpec.html?utm_source=openai))

The CrySL file points from the forbidden constructors to its four-argument `Con` event. **That is rule-specific guidance, not an Oracle statement that replacing the three-argument overload is universally correct or compatible.** Oracle’s PBE example itself uses the password-only constructor with a separate `PBEParameterSpec`. The CrySL threshold of 10,000 is likewise a rule constraint, not the constructor’s documented minimum. ([raw.githubusercontent.com](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CROSSINGTUD/Crypto-API-Rules/master/JavaCryptographicArchitecture/src/PBEKeySpec.crysl))

Oracle API documentation:  
https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/spec/PBEKeySpec.html

## Compatibility and migration

- Oracle states that PBE decryption must use the same salt and iteration count as encryption. Its JCA guide documents retrieving and encoding cipher parameters, and notes that `SealedObject` attaches encryption parameters to its encrypted contents. These are documented parameter-handling mechanisms, **not a general migration procedure** for a change of constructor or algorithm. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/security/java-cryptography-architecture-jca-reference-guide.html?utm_source=openai))
- The API describes the four-argument key length as a preference for variable-key-size ciphers and says the actual size depends on the provider. It does not promise that changing overloads preserves derived keys, persisted data, or wire compatibility. Provider, algorithm, parameter, and format details would be needed to assess compatibility. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/spec/PBEKeySpec.html?utm_source=openai))
- Oracle marks `PBEKeySpec` as available since Java 1.4. Algorithm and provider availability remain separate questions; the class’s presence alone does not establish support for a particular replacement algorithm or provider on a target platform. ([docs.oracle.com](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/api/java.base/javax/crypto/spec/PBEKeySpec.html?utm_source=openai))

Oracle JCA guide:  
https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/security/java-cryptography-architecture-jca-reference-guide.html

**Unresolved:** The sources do not identify the affected data format, provider, algorithm, target platforms, or detector implementation. They therefore do not establish a specific compatible migration path or verify how the reported analyzer resolved the call.
